_комментарий: English equipment library. Built by build_seo.py into /en/library/. Structure MUST mirror site/data/library.json: same category ids, same section order, same item ids — hreflang pairs and the anchor links depend on it.

categories.name: Output
categories.line: How the exhibition speaks to a person
categories.lead: Light, image, sound, vibration — everything that reaches a person. The most visible part of the budget and the most treacherous: a four-metre screen people walk past without looking loses to a spyglass with a queue in front of it.
categories.principle: Three numbers decide it: how much light is in the room, from what distance people look, and how many stand there at once. Not the diagonal, not the brand.

sections.name: Projection
sections.note: Light thrown at a surface. The only way to get a picture the size of a room, and the only one that lies down on something curved.

items.name: Installation laser projector
items.line: The workhorse. Runs for years and never asks for a lamp
items.what: Laser instead of a lamp: 20,000 hours without a change, instant start, mounts upside down if it has to. Lamp models are no longer specified for new exhibitions — not because they throw less light, but because someone has to change the lamp, and there is nobody to do it.
good: An image larger than a physical screen — from three metres up to a whole wall
A surface that is not flat: a model, a vault, a column, a façade
The screen has to disappear when off: a black wall instead of a black rectangle
bad: A room with windows and no blinds. Projection is the one technology sunlight kills outright, and no amount of lumens fixes that
Small type is needed: resolution divides across the area, and captions blur first
People walk between the viewer and the wall — there will be shadows
items.spec: The number that matters is not lumens but lumens per square metre at your actual ambient light. The second is contrast: in a bright room the winner is not the brightest projector but the one whose black stays black.

brands.note: верхний сегмент, купола и большие площади

items.name: Ultra-short-throw projector
items.line: You get the picture without the beam
items.what: Sits right against the surface and throws the image at almost a right angle. A person can walk up to the wall without blocking the frame with their own body — which is the whole point.
good: Interactive floors and tables: the visitor stands inside the image
Low ceilings, where a normal projector has nowhere to hang
People need to come right up to the surface and touch it
bad: An uneven surface: the sharper the angle, the more every bump shows
Large sizes — beyond three or four metres the geometry starts misbehaving

items.name: Rear projection
items.line: The projector hides behind the surface
items.what: Throws onto a translucent screen from behind. The viewer sees a glowing surface, never the machine or the beam, and casts no shadow — however many people crowd in.
good: A vitrine or window that should glow from within
Dense foot traffic right up against the image
The image has to sit together with a real object behind glass
bad: No room behind: you need a service recess half a metre deep or more
People look from far to the side — translucent materials have a narrower viewing angle than an ordinary screen

items.name: Mapping onto volume
items.line: Light lands along the facets of a real object
items.what: Not a device but a technique: the image is computed for the geometry of a model, a façade or a product. Needs an accurate model and blended projectors — in return the volume is real, not drawn.
good: There is a physical form — a site model, a building, a product, a landscape
The decision turns on scale: what stands where and how it connects
Several layers have to sit over one object — was, is, will be
bad: The object is small: for anything under a metre a plain screen beside it is cheaper and sharper
The model is not built yet — calibration is done against the real thing, not the drawing

sections.name: LED screens
sections.note: Not «another screen» but a construction set. The canvas is assembled from modules — tiles of roughly 50×50 cm. The module you pick decides the shape, the price, and whether it can be repaired in place.

items.name: Flat modular screen
items.line: A wall of any size that sunlight cannot bother
items.what: A module is a tile with its own LEDs, power and board. They build into a canvas of any shape, and a broken tile is replaced one tile at a time. One question is settled before purchase: is there half a metre behind for servicing, or must the modules come out from the front.
items.spec: Pixel pitch is the distance between LEDs in millimetres. A rough rule: comfortable viewing distance in metres roughly equals the pitch in millimetres. A 2.5 mm pitch means two and a half metres and further. Check on a sample in your own room rather than from the vendor's table: brightness and moiré only show in the flesh.
good: A bright room, an atrium, a window facing the street — sunlight is no obstacle
Non-standard proportions: a long ribbon, a vertical, a square across a wall
Round-the-clock operation: an LED does not fade the way a projector lamp does
The screen is an architectural element in its own right
bad: People come right up to it: at a 2 mm pitch the picture breaks into dots at about two metres, and «just take a finer pitch» is a different budget entirely
Deep black is needed in a dark room: an LED glows a little even when off
Weight and power: a 3×2 m canvas is already a question for the wall's load rating
Filming: without frequency sync the video will show banding

brands.note: широкий ряд, доступен в РФ, много б/у на рынке аренды
стандарт сценической аренды и виртуальных студий

items.name: Flexible modules
items.line: A screen that bends to fit
items.what: The same LEDs on a rubber backing: the canvas wraps a column, lies over a vault, follows the wave of a wall. Where a flat panel would leave a seam, this gives one continuous surface.
good: A column, an arch, a vault, a curved wall — anywhere a flat canvas would leave a seam
Shape matters more than resolution: from a distance the silhouette reads, not the pixel
Temporary builds: a flexible canvas is lighter and forgives an imprecise frame
bad: Fine pitch: the more flexible the backing, the coarser the available pitch
The radius is limited — get the minimum figure before designing the frame
Shorter service life than flat: bending works against the solder, and it does not enjoy being rehung again and again

brands.note: гибкие серии для колонн и сводов

items.name: Volumetric forms: sphere, cylinder, cube
items.line: This screen has no viewer's seat
items.what: Ready-made LED spheres, cylinders, cubes and rings. The image wraps the whole form, so the object works for people circling it and reads the same from a balcony and from below.
items.note_hw: Content for such a form is computed differently: flat video does not stretch onto a sphere without distortion. It needs an unwrap made for that exact geometry, and that is the work budgets routinely forget to include.
good: An atrium, a lobby, the centre of a room — a point people walk around
A globe, a planet, a core, a molecule — when the subject itself is round
An object that must read equally from a balcony and from below
bad: Text and diagrams: nothing is legible across curvature
A tight budget: a non-standard form always costs more than the same area of flat
Low ceilings — the object has to hang with clearance over people's heads

items.name: Kinetic LED screen
items.line: A canvas that moves through the air
items.what: Modules hang on winches and change position through the show: the screen parts, gathers, becomes a wave. Image and movement are one score — you cannot reproduce it with a video.
good: An opening, a launch, a show — an event with a beginning and a finale
An atrium with a high ceiling where the movement reads from below
An effect that cannot be reproduced by playing a video
bad: A permanent exhibition: winches need inspection regimes and permits, like any lifting gear
People underneath the rig — that is a safety calculation, not a preference
A quiet room: the drives are audible
items.spec: Treated as lifting equipment: load, secondary safeties, exclusion zone underneath. This is a matter of permits and inspection regime, not of design.

brands.note: лебёдки и светящиеся элементы, сценарное управление

sections.name: Panels
sections.note: A finished glowing plane, nothing to assemble. Everything projection cannot do: sunlight, small type, working without a day off.

items.name: Professional panel and video wall
items.line: Dull, dependable, legible
items.what: The industrial relative of a television: round-the-clock operation, portrait mounting, remote management, years without being switched off. A consumer TV in an exhibition lasts until its first summer.
good: Text, drawings and archive documents have to be read
The screen hangs for a long time and simply has to work
A modest budget: the best ratio of cost to legibility
bad: The job is impression, not reading: a panel does not create an event
A video wall of several panels: the bezels are always visible, and across a single image they read as a grid

brands.note: серия для витрин с высокой яркостью
широкая линейка, в том числе растянутые форматы

items.name: Transparent screen
items.line: Data over the real object
items.what: The image hangs on glass and the exhibit shows through. The original stays original while cutaways, labels and animation lie over it as a layer. Switch it off and only glass remains.
good: A vitrine holding an original that needs explaining without being covered
A cutaway, a diagram or a trajectory laid over a real product
When it is switched off, only glass should remain
bad: A bright room: a transparent screen is the first to lose to ambient light
A busy background behind the glass — the image loses legibility
A dense, saturated picture is needed: transparency works against contrast

sections.name: Volume and illusion
sections.note: Attempts to make an object look three-dimensional. The most marketing per square metre and the fewest honest caveats in the deck.

items.name: Pseudo-hologram: Pepper's ghost
items.line: A reflection in angled glass. Two hundred years and counting
items.what: The picture from a screen reflects in a semi-transparent film and appears to hang in mid-air. Nineteenth-century theatre knew this trick, and it is still the most dependable of the «holograms» — there is nothing in it to break.
good: A small object with one or two people gathered around it
A dark zone: the illusion is built on glowing in darkness
A floating effect without glasses and without teaching the visitor anything
bad: A delegation of twenty: the illusion holds only within a narrow angle
A bright room — the effect disappears entirely
Small captions: put them on a separate screen alongside

items.name: Holographic fan display
items.line: LEDs on spinning blades. Cheap and impossible to ignore
items.what: A strip of LEDs turns fast enough that the eye assembles the trail into a whole image hanging in the air. Installed in an hour, gangs into a wall — that is how the big «floating» objects are made.
good: A window, an entrance, a point that has to catch attention
A short bright image — a logo, an object, a sign
A wow effect on a small budget
Retail and events, where the unit moves from venue to venue
bad: A museum exhibition proper: a spinning part at hand height is a safety and noise question
A long story: neither the resolution nor the brightness carries content
Filming on a phone — the camera catches the strobing
Bright daylight washes the illusion out

items.name: Light-field display
items.line: Volume without glasses. The honest kind
items.what: The screen emits dozens of viewpoints at once: the eyes see different things and the object turns as you move your head. Sizes are still modest and the price matches — but this is real volume, not an illusion.
good: A single object to be examined from every side — a product, a molecule, a part
Volume with no glasses and no instructions
An exhibit for one or two people at a time
bad: A large audience and large sizes
A limited budget: for the same money you get an interactive 3D model on an ordinary screen, and people understand it just as well

brands.note: воксельный объём, вид с любой стороны

items.name: Autostereoscopic screen
items.line: Volume without glasses at panel money
items.what: An optical raster on an ordinary panel gives each eye its own pixels. Cheaper and larger than light-field; you pay in the narrow zone where the effect holds.
good: A vitrine or pylon that people approach one at a time
A product to be shown in volume without handing out glasses
Volume is wanted at the price of a panel, not of an installation
bad: A group: the viewing zone is narrow, one step aside and the volume falls apart
Horizontal resolution is divided between viewpoints: small type does not survive
Long viewing tires the eyes more than an ordinary screen

sections.name: Headsets and windows
sections.note: A picture tied to a head or to a device in the hand, rather than to a wall.

items.name: Virtual reality
items.line: The strongest impression and the longest queue
items.what: The headset closes off the world: a person ends up where they physically cannot be. One person at a time experiences it — and the whole schedule is counted from that number.
good: A place you cannot go: underground, in orbit, inside a ruined building, inside a body
A separate zone with a queue and an attendant
A session that can be sold on its own
bad: The main route of the exhibition: the queue forms and everything stops
No staff nearby: fitting, adjusting, disinfecting, removing
A school group on a timetable — the arithmetic does not work
items.spec: Work it out before purchase: a 4-minute session plus a minute to change over = 12 people an hour per headset. A group of 30 is two and a half hours on one unit.

items.name: Augmented reality on a device
items.line: A layer over the real room
items.what: A tablet or phone shows the camera feed with what the room does not contain laid over it: a building completed, a mechanism running, a character. Cheap in hardware, expensive in content.
good: Completing what has not survived: a ruin, a lost interior, a decommissioned machine
Showing the invisible over the visible: flows, cutaways, processes
An exhibit outside the building — a courtyard, a park, a street
bad: Relying on the visitor's phone with no guidance: only a fraction ever get it running
Poor connectivity and unwillingness to install an app
The exhibit has to work always: phones run flat, tablets get stolen

sections.name: Sound and body
sections.note: The underrated half of the impression. In specifications sound appears as «speakers — 4 pcs» and stops there.

items.name: Sound shower, directional audio
items.line: Audible here, silent one step away
items.what: Sound confined to a narrow zone: the visitor at the exhibit hears the story, a neighbour a metre away hears nothing, and nobody needs headphones. It cures the chief affliction of multimedia exhibitions — ten exhibits talking at once and none of them audible.
items.compare: Two different principles, and confusing them is expensive. A **parabolic dome** is an ordinary loudspeaker in a reflector: the sound is honest and full, the zone under the dome is about a metre across, and there is no distortion. An **ultrasonic parametric emitter** is a narrow beam of ultrasound that turns into sound in the air itself: the zone is far narrower and reaches further, but the bass is lost and speech sounds drier. For voice and atmosphere, the dome; for a pinpoint beam across a room, the parametric.
good: Several exhibits with sound in one room
A story that only the person standing here needs
Headphones are unwelcome — foot traffic or hygiene
bad: Full bass and enveloping sound are needed
High ceilings and heavy background noise: the zone smears
Visitors approach from several directions

brands.note: формирование звукового поля в большом зале

items.name: Installation audio and spatial sound
items.line: Sound that has a place in the room
items.what: Sources placed around the room give sound direction and distance: a footstep on the left, a rumble overhead, a voice from one point. Half the sense of presence is made here, not on the screen.
good: A large room with a single score — a panorama, a reconstruction, an immersion
People need to be led by sound rather than by arrows on the floor
There is a score with rhythm: silence, build, pause
bad: Scattered stands each with their own content — it will be a mess
A reverberant room with no acoustic treatment: fix the ceiling before buying speakers

items.name: Headphones and personal audio
items.line: When the story is long and personal
items.what: From a classic audio guide to streaming audio to the visitor's phone. The only way to deliver a long text, several languages and different depths from one and the same exhibit.
good: Many languages and different depths — children's, general, specialist
A story longer than two minutes
A quiet room where sound out loud would be out of place
bad: A family or a couple: headphones separate people who came together
A short caption — putting headphones on costs more than reading it
Servicing: charging, disinfecting, losses

brands.note: звук на телефон посетителя по Wi-Fi

items.name: Vibration, wind, heat, scent
items.line: What is remembered longer than the picture
items.what: Shakers in floors and benches, fans, heat, scent. Pennies next to screens, and it works disproportionately hard: the body remembers before the head does.
good: A moment that should be remembered by the body: a blast, a launch, a storm, a descent
Recreating an environment — the heat of a workshop, the damp of a trench, wind on a deck
A young audience: a physical impression lands before text does
bad: A constant background effect — people habituate within a minute and stop noticing
Scent: it stays in the room longer than intended, and not everyone likes it
Allergies and sensitivities — there must be a way to bypass the zone

brands.note: низкочастотные шейкеры под сиденья и пол

items.name: Controlled light
items.line: The cheapest way to change a scene
items.what: Light in an exhibition does not illuminate, it narrates: singles out, extinguishes, leads, sets the rhythm. It runs on the same cues as everything else at a fraction of any screen.
good: The route needs rhythm: darkness, flash, stillness
One original has to be picked out without touching the rest of the room
The budget has run out and the room is dull
bad: Scripted light fights the room's general lighting: separate the two from the start
Conservation requirements — lux levels and UV are agreed with the curator
Flashing and strobes: a medical constraint, not an aesthetic one

sections.name: Motion and matter
sections.note: Output that does not glow. An exhibition can answer physically: turn, open, change state.

items.name: Kinetics and mechanics
items.line: The exhibit genuinely moves
items.what: Actuators and mechanisms: a model opens out, a machine rotates, a cutaway parts. A different order of impression — the object is real, and it reads from the far end of the hall.
good: How a product is made: shown in section, with the real form opening up
A room where there are already too many screens and they have stopped working
An event visible from the far end of the hall
bad: Mechanics within reach of visitors: count the duty cycle and the pinch protection
A quiet room — drives are audible
Someone has to maintain it: moving things wear out, screens do not
items.spec: The one group in this whole library that needs a safety risk assessment: a moving part at a child's hand height is not a design question but an injury question.

items.name: Electronic ink
items.line: A label you can rewrite
items.what: The display draws power only while the image changes and reads like paper — at any angle, with nothing glowing into anyone's face. It cures an old museum ache: new attribution and a new language on the caption.
good: Labels and captions that change: new attribution, new language, rotation
A vitrine where a glowing screen would wreck the look
No power at the point: batteries last months
bad: Motion and video — refresh is slow by nature
Colour: colour models are noticeably paler and dearer
Large formats cost disproportionately much

brands.note: готовые панели с управлением по сети

items.name: Drone show
items.line: A screen the size of the sky
items.what: A swarm holds formation to a computed programme and draws three-dimensional figures in the air. The only way to get a picture hundreds of metres across with no structure at all — in many places it has already replaced fireworks: quieter, cleaner, repeatable.
items.note_hw: If someone's presentation still says «Intel Shooting Star», the document is out of date. Intel left this business in 2022, selling the division along with its fleet; shows today are flown by other companies on their own platforms.
good: An opening, an anniversary, a city celebration — an event under open sky
A scale that cannot be built: hundreds of metres in height and width
A place where fireworks are barred by noise, fire risk or animal welfare
bad: Wind and precipitation: the weather window is narrow, and a reserve date belongs in the contract rather than in conversation
Approvals: airspace, zone, time — that is weeks, not days
Indoors: a hall flies a handful of drones, not hundreds, and the effect is quite different
Fine graphics and text: resolution is the number of drones, and there are hundreds, not millions
items.spec: The resolution of the picture equals the number of drones. A hundred drones gives the outline of a recognisable symbol; a thousand gives a moving narrative. Budget follows the number of airframes and flying days, not the length of the show.

brands.note: дроны и ПО, продают платформу операторам

categories.name: Input
categories.lead: Fingers, hands, body, voice, mere presence. The cheapest line in the budget and the one that decides everything: this is where «interactive» parts company with «switched on».
categories.principle: The question is not how a person operates it, but how they worked out that they could. An exhibit that needs a plate of rules does not need a better sensor — it needs redesigning.

sections.name: Touch
sections.note: Everyone gets it: people learned on their phones. And it is over-specified — touch works for one person and barely works for a group.

items.name: Capacitive touch
items.line: Like a phone, only large
items.what: Film or glass sensing a finger through an electric field. High precision, honest multi-touch, and the glass can be thick — touch reads straight through, so the exhibit survives a blow.
good: A vitrine where things are touched through protective glass
Confident multi-touch: a map two people rotate and stretch together
The surface has to stay perfectly flat and clean
bad: Visitors in gloves — in a northern museum in winter that is half the room
Very large sizes: the bigger the film, the more temperamental and expensive
Wet hands and water droplets produce phantom touches

items.name: Infrared frame
items.line: Cheap, large, works in mittens
items.what: A frame around the edge catches the broken beam. It responds to anything — finger, glove, pointer, elbow. In a northern museum in winter that is half the room.
good: Large diagonals, where capacitive touch costs as much as the screen
Gloves, mittens, children in winter coats
A limited budget and a large surface
bad: The frame stands proud of the glass — dirt collects and it does not look sleek
Direct sunlight and strong infrared sources confuse it
Lower precision: small interface elements cannot be hit

items.name: Lidar touch on any surface
items.line: Touch where touch cannot exist
items.what: A scanner casts a plane of light above a surface and detects where it is crossed. It turns a wall, a vitrine, a model or a floor into a touch surface — no film, no frame, no intervention in the surface itself.
good: A historic surface that no equipment may be attached to
Projection on a wall or floor that becomes interactive
A very large area: the price barely rises with size
bad: Calibration lasts until the device is first nudged — mount it immovably
There is one plane: touch is read in two dimensions, pressure is not distinguished
People standing in the plane of the beam occlude one another

items.name: Off-the-shelf touch monitor
items.line: Do not assemble it from parts — buy it whole
items.what: Glass, touch layer and electronics already built and tested together. A kit of frame, panel and computer is cheaper on paper, takes longer to commission, and when it fails there turns out to be nobody to blame.
good: An ordinary interactive stand with no unusual geometry
Time is short: a finished monitor goes in within an hour, an assembly takes a week
Many identical points: ten identical all-in-ones are simpler to service
No in-house engineer: one warranty on one product rather than four separate invoices
bad: A non-standard size or shape, or flush mounting into joinery
Very large diagonals: off-the-shelf options run out and the price climbs steeply
The glass must be thick or armoured — then you need separate components

brands.note: рабочая лошадь: сенсорные мониторы и большие панели, доступны в РФ

sections.name: Physical action
sections.note: Real objects that get turned and pressed. They lose to touch on flexibility and win on everything else: understood without words, work for a group, remembered by the hands.

items.name: Real operating controls
items.line: A lever, a handwheel, a toggle, a helm
items.what: Industrial buttons and grips, taken off real machinery or made to match. Understood without a word — by a child, and by the visitor who keeps away from screens.
good: An exhibition about machinery: you should operate it with what actually operated it
Children and older visitors — understood without a single word
The exhibit must survive a million presses and a school outing
bad: The content changes often: each scenario needs its own object
A complex choice among many options — that calls for a screen
A cramped room: a physical console takes space, a screen does not
items.spec: Work out the duty cycle in advance: an industrial button lasts millions of cycles, a consumer one tens of thousands. At two thousand visitors a day, that is the difference between five years and two months.

items.name: Rotary knob and encoder
items.line: One movement everybody understands
items.what: Turning is the most natural gesture after pressing: it is how you leaf through years, move through a cutaway, change scale. A knob gives what a screen cannot — resistance under the fingers.
items.note_hw: The classic of the genre, the Griffin PowerMate, went out of production in 2018 — if it appears in a specification, that document was written from old templates. Living replacements: Binepad BNR1, Contour ShuttleXpress, and for a permanent installation better an industrial encoder rated for a million turns.
good: A timeline: scroll through a year, an era, a stage of a process
A cutaway or layers: move through an object in a single gesture
A visitor who struggles to hit a small element on a screen
Physical precision is wanted — a screen does not give it
bad: Choosing among many options: that needs a list, not a knob
Consumer models wear out quickly under footfall — count the duty cycle
The meaning of the turn has to be shown: without a hint half the visitors miss it

items.name: An object as a key
items.line: Put a thing down and the exhibition answers
items.what: A real object with a marker underneath: the system knows what was placed and how it is turned. The interaction becomes physical and collective — everyone holds their own.
good: Comparing several things: put them side by side and see the connection
Group work: each person holds their own object
A link is needed between the original in the hand and the data on the screen
bad: Objects get lost and broken — budget for consumption and spares
It does not work without staff if the objects are valuable
It copes poorly with crowds: someone has to put them back

items.name: Visitor card, RFID and NFC
items.line: The exhibition knows who is standing there
items.what: A ticket or wristband with a tag. Touch it and the exhibit speaks your language and resumes where you left off. At the end of the route it hands you a personal summary of what you saw and gathered.
good: A long route with a running narrative and accumulation
Many languages without a single language button
A trace after the visit: an email, a page, a link to what was gathered
bad: Free entry with no ticket — there is nobody to hand out cards
Personal data: tying this to a visitor's identity needs a legal basis
Cards get taken away and lost, a constant running cost

items.name: Weight, pressure and environmental sensors
items.line: The exhibition feels physical effort
items.what: Load cells, pressure mats, rotation sensors. Cheap and utterly honest: apply force and something happens. Nothing to explain.
good: Comparing effort or mass: lift, press, pull
A mat by an exhibit that starts the scene when someone steps on it
The exhibit has to work for a person of any height and any hands
bad: Precise measurement as the content: consumer sensors drift over time
Constant load wears the mechanics faster than the electronics

sections.name: Body and gesture
sections.note: Nothing to touch and nothing to explain. The most striking group and the most temperamental: the less contact there is, the harder it is to realise you are in control at all.

items.name: Depth camera and skeleton tracking
items.line: The system sees posture and movement
items.what: The camera measures distance to every point in frame and builds a skeleton: where the arms are, which way the lean goes, how many people. The basis of everything involving waving, copying and dodging.
items.note_hw: Important for the specification: Microsoft ended production of the Azure Kinect DK in 2023 and passed the technology to partners. The direct successor is the Orbbec Femto Bolt, on the same depth technology with a compatible programming interface: Kinect code ports across with almost no changes. If your specification still says «Kinect», that is a red flag — the document was written from old templates.
good: Whole-body movement: copy it, dodge it, dance it, hold still
Several people at once in front of one exhibit
Counting the queue and knowing whether anyone is there at all
bad: Bright sunlight: infrared depth cameras go blind outdoors
A dense crowd — skeletons merge
Dark clothing and reflective surfaces leave holes in the measurement

brands.note: стереокамеры; с 2025 самостоятельная компания вне Intel
глубина плюс нейросеть в самой камере

items.name: Hand tracking
items.line: Fingers in the air, no gloves
items.what: The device looks up and sees hands down to individual fingers: a virtual object can be picked up, turned and taken apart by hand. Not one touch — and it looks like magic.
good: Hygiene above all: medicine, a children's museum, epidemic restrictions
An action on an object: turn it, open it, dismantle it
The exhibit should look like magic
bad: The working volume is small — about a cubic metre above the device, no more
People do not think to raise their hands: the screen must hint with movement
Arms tire within a minute — the scenario has to be short

items.name: Presence sensor
items.line: The exhibit wakes up by itself
items.what: An infrared or radar sensor notices someone nearby. The cheapest part in the whole specification and one of the most useful: the exhibit calls out, and in an empty room it saves its own life.
good: The exhibit should call out rather than wait to be pressed
Saving panel and projector hours through the empty times
Honest footfall statistics by zone
bad: A through corridor: it triggers on everyone walking past
Radar sees through a thin partition — the next room will keep waking yours
An abrupt start startles people: bring it up gently

items.name: Reading brain activity
items.line: An exhibit you operate by doing nothing
items.what: A light headband reads brain activity and tells states apart — concentration, relaxation, a spike of attention. It does not read thoughts, and saying so plainly on the exhibit is already half the scenario.
items.note_hw: Expectations have to be lowered in advance. Consumer models give a few channels and distinguish two or three states with a delay of seconds. Anything promising more from a consumer headband is marketing.
good: The subject of the exhibition is the brain itself, attention, meditation, consciousness
A contest exhibit: who can relax or concentrate faster
An attended zone where staff fit the device and explain it
A conversation about the technology is wanted, not just an effect
bad: Free flow: the headband is fitted, tuned and wiped down — that takes minutes
Hygiene and hair: electrode contact depends on hairstyle and gel
A guaranteed result: for some people the signal simply does not read
Data about a person's state is a legal question again, if it is stored

brands.note: обруч с сухими электродами, есть поток данных для разработчика
открытая платформа, полный доступ к сырым данным
открытый протокол: связывает прибор со сценой

sections.name: Camera and algorithm
sections.note: An ordinary camera plus software that understands the frame. The only group where you need a lawyer before you need an engineer.

items.name: Computer vision
items.line: A camera that understands the frame
items.what: An industrial camera and a neural network: tells objects apart, counts people, recognises a gesture or a drawing. One camera replaces a dozen sensors and does what sensors cannot do at all.
good: The visitor draws, assembles or builds — and the system understands it
Counting flow and heat-mapping the room: where people stand, where they walk past
Reacting to an object someone has brought with them
bad: Light changes through the day — a model trained in the morning errs by evening
Guaranteed accuracy is required: vision is probabilistic by nature
Filming people: a legal basis and clear notice are obligatory

brands.note: промышленные камеры, долгий срок поставки моделей

items.name: Face and emotion recognition
items.line: Technically easy, legally expensive
items.what: Age, gender, emotion, identity — from a face. It works reliably and costs little. We install it rarely and discuss it separately: biometrics are a special category of personal data, and the rules are stricter than they look in a vendor demo.
good: Anonymous statistics with no frames retained: how many people, of roughly what age
A narrative where recognition is the subject of the exhibition and the visitor has agreed to it
bad: Storing biometrics without written consent is a straightforward breach
A young audience: a further level of requirements
A recognition error in public humiliates a person, and that is not a technical problem
items.warn: This is where we usually talk clients out of it. Nine times in ten the actual job is done by anonymous silhouette counting with no faces at all — cheaper, more reliable and with no legal consequences.

items.name: Voice
items.line: Ask out loud, get an answer
items.what: This only became usable recently: current models understand living speech rather than memorised commands, and answer from the content of the exhibition rather than from a list of ten questions.
good: Open questions that cannot be anticipated
Accessibility: a visitor who finds reading or reaching a screen difficult
Dialogue as the subject itself — a conversation with a character, a witness, an expert
bad: A noisy room: recognition fails first, and the visitor is the one who feels at fault
Many people are shy about speaking aloud among strangers — a semi-enclosed zone helps
The model's answers must be bounded by the museum's content, or it will invent

brands.note: распознавание и синтез, работает в РФ

items.name: Positioning within the building
items.line: The exhibition knows where you are standing
items.what: A tag on the ticket and receivers around the building: the system knows who is where, to within tens of centimetres. Content arrives by location, and you get a map of the routes people actually walk.
good: A large floor area with a running narrative and a personal route
An audio guide that knows for itself which exhibit you are standing at
Route analytics: where people actually walk and where the dead zone is
bad: A small exhibition: a presence sensor is tens of times cheaper and does the same job
Metal and thick walls disrupt radio
Tying it to a visitor's identity — a legal question once more

items.name: Draw it and bring it to life
items.line: A visitor's drawing swims onto the shared screen
items.what: A table with paper and a scanner: colour a sheet, place it under the camera, and ten seconds later your character is swimming among everyone else's. It holds a child without fail, and the sheet goes home.
good: A children's and family audience: it works without fail
A trace after the visit — the sheet stays with the visitor
A shared screen accumulating the contribution of everyone who passed through that day
bad: Consumables: paper, pencils, and somebody has to restock them
Moderation — anything at all may end up on a sheet, so a filter or staff are needed
An adult audience without children walks straight past

items.name: Three-dimensional scanning
items.line: How a real object gets into the scene
items.what: A laser scanner or photogrammetry turns an object, a room or a site into an accurate model. Modelling a building from scratch costs more and convinces less than scanning it in a day.
good: There is an original, a building or a site that has to be shown truthfully
Projection onto a model: the unwrap is computed from the scan, not the drawing
The object is about to change or disappear — the scan remains for good
Verified room geometry is needed before equipment is installed
bad: Shiny, transparent and black surfaces scan poorly — glass and polish need matting spray or hand repair
A raw scan is not fit to show: millions of points have to be cleaned and simplified, and that work exceeds the scanning itself
Fine jewellery-scale detail: that needs a different class of instrument
items.spec: Scanning is one or two days; processing is weeks. Budgets routinely include the first and forget the second.

brands.note: сканирование лидаром айфона, черновая съёмка на месте

sections.name: The visitor's own device
sections.note: A phone does not fit the three categories: it is input, output and processing at once. And it is already in everyone's pocket — the cheapest equipment here and the hardest to use well.

items.name: The phone as a complete system
items.line: Input, output and computing at once — at someone else's expense
items.what: A phone already has touch, camera, microphone, sensors, lidar on the higher models, a screen, sound and enough power for augmented reality. Nothing spent on hardware. You pay elsewhere: every step before launch loses people.
items.spec: Count the funnel honestly. A hundred people reach the exhibit; half notice the invitation; a third of those get their phone out; a handful install an app. A web page with no installation changes that arithmetic several times over, and is almost always the right choice.
good: An exhibit outside the building: a courtyard, a park, a street, a city route
A personal route and something to take away: a photo, a result, a link
Many languages with no button — the phone knows its owner's language
A temporary exhibition where there is nothing to build but something to tell
Accessibility: their own screen, their own type size, their own vision settings
bad: As the main exhibit on the route: some visitors will simply not take a phone out
Counting on an app being installed for a single visit — almost nobody will
An older audience, and school groups without phones
Weak connectivity: the guest network has to be tested beforehand, not on opening day
Battery: a long scenario drains it, and the museum will get the blame

brands.note: лучший трекинг, лидар на старших моделях
Android, работает без установки через Scene Viewer
дополненная реальность прямо в браузере, без приложения
готовая платформа аудиогидов, бесплатна для музеев

categories.name: Processing
categories.line: What nobody sees and everything rests on
categories.lead: Machines, engines, network, room control. None of it appears in a single photograph of an exhibition, which is why it gets cut from the budget first. A year later it is exactly this part that decides whether the place runs or stands idle.
categories.principle: Acceptance in two questions: does the exhibit come up on one button pressed by an attendant, and can the museum change the text itself. Two nos and you have bought a contractor in perpetuity, not a system.

sections.name: Machines
sections.note: The hardware it all runs on. Chosen not by power but by who will restart it, and how.

items.name: Media player appliance
items.line: A box that simply plays
items.what: No moving parts and no operating system in the usual sense: switch it on and the schedule runs. It does not hang, does not update at the wrong moment, and does not show a desktop in the middle of a gallery.
good: A film or a schedule with no interactivity
Many identical points: ten screens with the same content
Nobody to service it — you need a thing that simply does not break
bad: Genuine interactivity and real-time 3D — beyond it
Content that depends on external data and logic

items.name: Industrial computer
items.line: No fan, no dust, no surprises
items.what: A sealed case, passive cooling, and years of the same model staying available. That last point matters more than speed: in three years you will need exactly the same one.
items.note_hw: An ordinary office build inside a plinth survives until its first summer: dust settles on the fan, the temperature climbs, and the machine throttles out on the busiest day. This is the commonest mistake in ready-made specifications.
good: An exhibit inside a sealed box or in a dusty room
Running for months without being switched off
A guarantee that the same unit can be bought in three years
bad: Heavy real-time graphics: that needs a discrete card and active cooling
A one-week trade show — overpaying

brands.note: линейка NUC, перешедшая к ASUS от Intel

items.name: Single-board computer
items.line: Thirty dollars instead of three hundred
items.what: A computer the size of a palm covers half the points in an exhibition: a sensor, a button, sound on a trigger, lighting, simple video. Everywhere a full PC would otherwise stand «just in case».
good: Many small points: a sensor, a button, a lamp, an audio response
The exhibit hides in a plinth with no room and no ventilation
Spares matter: keeping three on a shelf is cheap
A link to the physical world — sensors and actuators connect directly
bad: Real-time 3D and heavy video: not for this
The memory card is the weak point; with frequent hard power-offs it dies first — cured by booting from an SSD and a read-only filesystem
Supply in batches: in a shortage, price and lead time triple
items.spec: The main question is not performance but how it survives being switched off at the mains at closing time. A board configured to read from a protected partition lasts years; a stock install on a memory card lasts months.

brands.note: стандарт: документация, сообщество, промышленные сроки поставки
то же, но с нейросетями на борту
если нужна только физика, без операционной системы

items.name: Graphics workstation
items.line: When the picture is computed right now
items.what: A professional graphics card and several outputs. Needed where the image is not played back but born: real-time 3D, reaction to a person, synchronised screens from one scene.
good: An interactive 3D scene reacting to visitors
Several projectors from one source, blended into a single field
Content that depends on data and changes on the fly
bad: It plays a film — several times the money for nothing
No ventilation in the plinth: this machine runs genuinely hot

items.name: Neural networks on site
items.line: Computes here, sends nothing anywhere
items.what: The module runs recognition right in the room, with no internet and no cloud. Frames never leave the museum — and half the legal questions vanish before they arise.
good: Recognition where data may not be sent outside
Unstable internet, or none at all
Latency is critical: the response must be immediate
bad: The heaviest models: on-site capacity is always less than cloud capacity
A model that needs frequent updates — on site that is manual work

brands.note: камера и вычислитель в одном корпусе

items.name: The operating system of the room
items.line: A dull choice that echoes for two years
items.what: Windows, macOS or Linux is decided once and determines who can service the exhibition. Chosen not by taste but by what the required software runs on, and who will fix it on a Saturday afternoon.
items.compare: **Windows** runs nearly everything: media servers, TouchDesigner, Unity and Unreal builds, drivers for any hardware. The price is updates that arrive at the wrong moment and reboot the gallery; cured by a long-term-servicing edition, not by a «defer» checkbox. **macOS** is reliable and quiet, good for audio and video, but the software choice is narrower and it is harder to put a machine in a plinth and leave it for five years. **Linux** is free, does not reboot itself and is ideal for players and single-board machines; professional media servers for it are rare.
good: Windows: interactivity, 3D, unusual hardware, media servers
macOS: audio, video, colour accuracy, a small quiet point
Linux: schedules, players, single-board machines, anything that must simply not fall over
bad: A mixed estate of three systems in one gallery: there will be nobody to service it
Choosing by the contractor's habit rather than by the software — the commonest reason a museum ends up tied to one supplier
items.warn: Whatever is chosen, disable automatic updates and automatic sleep, set the scenario to launch on boot, and enable automatic login. Test it at acceptance the simple way: pull the power and see whether the exhibit comes back up on its own, with no keyboard.

brands.note: редакция без внезапных обновлений, для киосков

sections.name: Media servers
sections.note: A class of its own: machine and software together. The job is to bring a dozen images and outputs into one governable picture.

items.name: Media server
items.line: One brain for a whole projection wall
items.what: Feeds a dozen outputs, blends projectors into one field, corrects geometry for a curved surface and holds it all to a timeline. More than two projectors without one is a zoo.
good: Several projectors into one field: a panorama, a dome, a vault
Mapping onto volume with exact geometry
The show runs to a schedule and must start itself
bad: One screen with a film — an order of magnitude more than needed
Deep interactivity: a media server is strong at playback, not at logic

brands.note: верхний сегмент, сцена и большие площадки
показ и маппинг в одной системе

items.name: Warping and geometry correction
items.line: So the seam cannot be seen
items.what: Software works out from camera shots how to distort each image so the projectors merge into one field. Recomputed in minutes rather than overnight — which matters, because buildings move and equipment shifts.
good: More than one projector on one surface
A surface that is not flat: a vault, a dome, a corner, a model
Calibration will have to be repeated — buildings move and equipment shifts
bad: One projector on a flat wall — nothing is needed
No way to place a camera where the viewer stands

brands.note: сшивка, в том числе внутри медиасерверов

sections.name: Engines and environments
sections.note: Where the content gets made. The choice decides not how it looks but who will be able to change it later.

items.name: Unity
items.line: The workhorse of interactive exhibits
items.what: The standard for museum interactivity: real-time 3D, any sensor, builds for anything from a gallery screen to a headset to a phone. More specialists on the market than for any other tool on this list, and a contractor who is easy to replace.
good: An interactive exhibit with real logic and state
One body of content across several devices: gallery, headset, phone
You want a contractor who can easily be replaced later
bad: A simple film — overkill
Top-grade photorealistic architecture: Unreal is stronger there

items.name: Unreal Engine
items.line: When the credibility of the image decides it
items.what: The strongest lighting and materials out of the box. Chosen where the image must be indistinguishable from a photograph: architecture, interiors, landscape, a product at advertising quality.
good: Architecture and territory that must look real
A large world with distant views
Material matters in itself: metal, fabric, glass
bad: Modest hardware: the machine requirements are noticeably higher
Simple logic on a small screen — heavy for the job

items.name: TouchDesigner
items.line: An environment for things that never repeat
items.what: A node-based environment for generative graphics and live reaction to data. Unity builds a scene; TouchDesigner builds a flow — a picture born of movement and sound that never looks the same twice.
good: Generative content: an image born from data or movement
Many inputs and outputs at once: cameras, sensors, projectors, sound
Fast rework on site, during the install
bad: Classic game logic with levels and states
A wide choice of replacement contractors: there are markedly fewer specialists

items.name: Notch and Resolume
items.line: Tools for live performance
items.what: Notch computes real-time effects inside media servers; Resolume drives playback and mapping from a desk. Both are about an event and a person at the controls, not an exhibition running unattended.
good: An event, an opening, a show on a façade
The effect has to react to a live signal — sound, camera, operator
You need a desk that a person sits at and drives the show by hand
bad: A permanent exhibition with no operator
Complex branching interaction logic

brands.note: эффекты в реальном времени, работает внутри медиасерверов

items.name: Creative coding
items.line: Here the graphics are written, not assembled
items.what: Open environments where the picture is born of code and data: sound visualisation, generative patterns, reaction to the flow of visitors. No licences required, and happy on modest hardware.
good: Generative content: a pattern out of data, sound, movement
A small budget with no software licences
A prototype that has to be tested in a day before a decision is made
A long life: open source is not withdrawn or moved to a subscription
bad: A complex scene with 3D and physics — faster in a game engine
Handing the project to another contractor: markedly fewer specialists
Vendor support is wanted — by definition it does not exist

brands.note: самый низкий порог входа, огромное сообщество
то же в браузере: работает на любом экране без установки
узловая среда, сильна в работе с железом

sections.name: Signal and operations
sections.note: First thing struck from the budget, first thing remembered in year two. Pays for itself with one call-out that never had to happen.

items.name: Signal distribution
items.line: Distance decides more than you would think
items.what: An ordinary cable works to about fifteen metres; beyond that you need twisted pair with transmitters, fibre, or the network. Settled while the walls are open. Afterwards — expensive.
good: Machine in the rack room, screen in the gallery: separating them is right
Many sources and many screens with switching
A historic building where chasing walls is not allowed — the network saves you
bad: Network transport adds latency, and interactivity does not forgive it
Cheap extenders produce dropouts that take months to track down

items.name: Room control
items.line: One button for the whole exhibition
items.what: Switches on to a schedule in the morning, shuts down at night, and gives the attendant one sensible panel instead of ten remotes. This is what decides whether the museum opens without an engineer.
good: More than five devices in a room
Opening and closing to a schedule, with nobody present
An attendant has to be able to restart an exhibit unaided
bad: One or two exhibits: a socket with a timer does the same
No trained person at all: this too needs a minimum of competence

brands.note: звук, изображение и управление в одной системе

items.name: Monitoring and remote access
items.line: Learn about the fault before the visitor does
items.what: The system reports that an exhibit has gone dark, a lamp has reached end of life, or a machine rebooted overnight. Without it you hear about the fault from an online review.
good: An exhibition of more than one room
The contractor is not in your city
Equipment under warranty, where running hours have to be evidenced
bad: Security will not permit external access — settle that beforehand, not after install

items.name: Content management system
items.line: So text can change without the contractor
items.what: The panel through which the museum edits captions itself, swaps photographs and adds a language. The most important line in the acceptance list and the most frequently absent.
good: The content will change — and it will
Several languages, added over time
Temporary exhibitions inside a permanent display
bad: A one-off exhibit that will never change — rare, but it happens
Nobody to use it: a panel without a trained member of staff is dead
items.warn: Demand it explicitly at acceptance: have a member of museum staff change a caption on an exhibit, in front of you, without phoning the contractor. If that is impossible, you have bought a dependency.

items.name: Machine synchronisation
items.line: So adjacent screens stay in step
items.what: Each machine runs on its own clock, and within a minute of playback the drift is visible to the eye. Synchronisation binds them to a common time: frame to frame, sound to image.
good: A panorama or wall assembled from several machines
Sound and image from different sources that have to coincide
The show loops all day and must not drift apart
bad: One machine for everything — nothing is needed
Screens far apart and never seen at the same time

items.name: Backup and recovery
items.line: A plan for the day it does break
items.what: An image of every machine, a copy of the content and a written recovery procedure. Not equipment but a clause in the contract — and without it, replacing a burnt-out computer turns from an hour into a week.
good: An exhibition that has to open tomorrow whatever happens
The contractor may leave the market — the museum will not
Uniform equipment: one image covers ten machines
bad: Not a single person who will follow the procedure — then you need a service contract
items.warn: Ask for these separately at acceptance: machine images, content source files and a printed recovery procedure. This is what the museum owns outright, rather than borrows for the duration.
